node_definition.done_when: First, at your base, run tests/test_obligations_snapshot_is_published.py and record in the manifest whether test_the_snapshot_carries_the_derivation_over_unmodified_files and test_a_slice_equals_the_derivation_over_the_same_files fail, with their output. payload_for in reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py builds each review duty through _review_duty_item in reckon/crew/obligations.py, the function the derivation uses, so a snapshot's duty list equals the derivation's over the same files, including the head field and the reviewed head when the two differ. Both parity cases pass at head. A new case in tests/test_obligations_snapshot_is_published.py sets a run's worktree head past the revision its stored review recorded, in a temporary repository and configuration home, and asserts the snapshot's duty and the derivation's both read review-missing and name the same two heads. The gate is tests/test_obligations_snapshot_is_published.py, tests/test_review_obligation_reads_the_head.py and every test file under tests/ that names obligation_snapshot, found by a text search; list them in the manifest. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
